about.title: About Roth IRA Calculator - Tax-Free Retirement Planning Tool
about.description: The Roth IRA Calculator is a specialized retirement planning tool designed to help you calculate the tax-free growth potential of your Roth Individual Retirement Account. Unlike Traditional IRAs, Roth IRA contributions are made with after-tax dollars, but qualified withdrawals in retirement are completely tax-free. This calculator helps you project your Roth IRA balance at retirement and compare the benefits of tax-free growth versus traditional tax-deferred retirement accounts.

faq.q: What are the 2024 Roth IRA contribution limits?
faq.a: For 2024, you can contribute up to $7,000 to a Roth IRA ($8,000 if you're 50 or older). However, contribution limits phase out for high earners: $138,000-$153,000 for single filers and $218,000-$228,000 for married filing jointly.

faq.q: When can I withdraw from my Roth IRA tax-free?
faq.a: Contributions can be withdrawn tax and penalty-free at any time. Earnings can be withdrawn tax and penalty-free after age 59½ and the account has been open for at least 5 years. Earlier earnings withdrawals may incur taxes and penalties.

faq.q: Should I choose Roth IRA over Traditional IRA?
faq.a: Choose Roth IRA if you expect to be in a higher tax bracket in retirement, want tax-free withdrawals, or prefer no required minimum distributions. Choose Traditional IRA if you want current tax deductions and expect lower retirement tax rates.

faq.q: What is a backdoor Roth IRA conversion?
faq.a: A backdoor Roth allows high-income earners who exceed Roth IRA income limits to contribute to a non-deductible Traditional IRA and then convert it to a Roth IRA. This strategy requires careful tax planning and professional guidance.
